1.overview: After Moab rebels, Ahaziah is injured and sends messengers to consult Baal-zebub of Ekron; Elijah intercepts them and declares that the king will die. Ahaziah’s captains twice demand that Elijah come down and are consumed by fire, but a third captain approaches humbly, and Elijah repeats the LORD’s verdict before Ahaziah dies and Jehoram succeeds him.

2.overview: Elijah travels with Elisha from Gilgal through Bethel and Jericho to the Jordan, where he parts the waters and is taken up in a whirlwind; Elisha receives Elijah’s cloak and crosses the river after requesting a double portion of his spirit. Recognized as Elijah’s successor, Elisha heals Jericho’s water, then curses a group of boys at Bethel, where two bears maul forty-two of them, before he travels to Mount Carmel and returns to Samaria.

sections.heading: Elijah and Elisha Travel to the Jordan

3.overview: Jehoram of Israel removes Baal’s sacred pillar but continues the sins of Jeroboam, and he joins Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom in a campaign against Moab. When the allied armies run out of water, Elisha prophesies water and victory; the Moabites mistake the water for blood, are defeated, and withdraw after their king offers his son as a burnt offering.

sections.heading: Elisha’s Prophecy of Water and Victory

4.overview: Elisha multiplies a widow’s oil to pay her debt, promises a son to a hospitable woman of Shunem, and later restores the woman’s dead son to life. During a famine, he makes poisonous stew safe and multiplies twenty barley loaves to feed a hundred men with food left over.

5.overview: Naaman, an Aramean commander with leprosy, goes to Elisha in Samaria and is cleansed after washing seven times in the Jordan; he acknowledges the God of Israel and Elisha refuses his gifts. Gehazi secretly takes gifts from Naaman, and Elisha confronts him and declares that Naaman’s leprosy will cling to Gehazi and his descendants.

sections.heading: Naaman Is Cleansed in the Jordan
Gehazi Takes Gifts and Is Punished

6.overview: Elisha makes a borrowed axe head float, repeatedly warns Israel’s king of Aramean plans, and leads an Aramean force from Dothan to Samaria, where Israel’s king feeds and releases them. Later, Ben-hadad besieges Samaria, famine brings extreme suffering, and Israel’s king threatens Elisha before declaring that the calamity comes from the LORD.

sections.heading: The Siege and Famine of Samaria

7.overview: Elisha announces that food prices will fall in Samaria by the next day, but the king’s officer doubts the prediction and is told he will see the abundance without eating it. Four lepers find the abandoned Aramean camp, report it to the king, and the people plunder its provisions; food prices fall as prophesied, and the officer dies after being trampled at the gate.

sections.heading: Elisha’s Prediction and the Officer’s Doubt
The Lepers Find the Abandoned Camp
The King Sends Scouts and the City Takes Plunder
The Officer’s Death Confirms the Prediction

8.overview: The Shunammite woman returns after seven years in Philistine territory and, as Gehazi recounts Elisha’s miracles to the king, receives her house, land, and its produce back. In Damascus, Elisha predicts Hazael’s rise and violence against Israel; the chapter then records Jehoram and Ahaziah’s reigns in Judah, including Edom’s revolt and Joram’s wounding at Ramoth-gilead.

9.overview: Elisha sends a young prophet to anoint Jehu king of Israel and charge him with bringing judgment on Ahab’s house, and Jehu’s commanders proclaim him king. Jehu kills Joram at Naboth’s property, Ahaziah dies after fleeing, and Jezebel is thrown from a window at Jezreel, fulfilling the prophetic word about her death.

10.overview: Jehu secures the deaths of Ahab’s descendants in Samaria and Jezreel, kills Ahaziah’s relatives, and destroys Baal worship in Israel. The LORD grants Jehu’s dynasty four generations on the throne, but Jehu retains Jeroboam’s golden calves, and Hazael takes territory from Israel before Jehu’s death.

sections.heading: Ahab’s sons killed in Samaria and Jezreel
Jehu kills Ahaziah’s relatives and Ahab’s survivors
Jehu’s incomplete reform and final years

11.overview: Athaliah kills the royal heirs, but Jehosheba hides Joash in the house of the LORD while Athaliah rules for six years. In the seventh year, Jehoiada arranges Joash’s coronation, has Athaliah put to death, renews the covenants, and leads the people in destroying Baal’s temple before Joash takes the throne.

12.overview: Joash reigns in Jerusalem and, while instructed by Jehoiada, does what is right, but the high places remain. After the priests fail to repair the temple, Joash establishes a collection system that funds the repairs; later he sends temple and royal treasures to Hazael of Aram, and his servants kill him at Beth-millo before Amaziah succeeds him.

13.overview: Jehoahaz and his son Jehoash reign over Israel, continuing Jeroboam’s sins while facing Aramean oppression; the LORD grants relief and remains gracious to Israel because of his covenant. As Elisha nears death, he predicts limited victories over Aram for Jehoash, and a dead man is revived when his body touches Elisha’s bones before Jehoash recovers Israelite cities from Ben-hadad.

14.overview: Amaziah rules Judah, executes his father’s murderers according to the law, defeats Edom, and is captured after challenging Jehoash of Israel, who defeats Judah and plunders Jerusalem. After Amaziah’s death, Azariah succeeds him, while Jeroboam II rules Israel, restores its borders in keeping with the LORD’s word through Jonah, and dies, leaving the throne to Zechariah.

sections.heading: Jehoash Defeats Judah and Plunders Jerusalem

15.overview: Azariah rules Judah, but lives apart with leprosy while Jotham governs; in Israel, Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah, and Pekah succeed one another through coups, and Menahem pays tribute to Assyria. Assyria takes northern territories and their people, Hoshea kills Pekah, and Jotham rules Judah, rebuilds the temple’s Upper Gate, and faces pressure from Aram and Israel.

16.overview: Ahaz becomes king of Judah, practices idolatry, and appeals to Tiglath-pileser of Assyria when Rezin of Aram and Pekah of Israel attack Jerusalem; Assyria captures Damascus and kills Rezin. After visiting Damascus, Ahaz replaces the temple altar with a new one modeled on its altar, alters temple furnishings, and dies, leaving the throne to Hezekiah.

17.overview: Hoshea’s failed revolt against Assyria ends with Samaria’s capture and Israel’s exile, which the chapter attributes to Israel’s persistent idolatry and rejection of the Lord’s warnings. Assyria resettles Samaria with peoples from other lands, who adopt a mixed worship of the Lord and their own gods that continues among their descendants.

sections.heading: The Lord’s Covenant and Persistent Idolatry

18.overview: Hezekiah becomes king of Judah, removes idolatrous objects, trusts the LORD, and resists Assyria as Samaria falls and its people are exiled. Sennacherib invades Judah and demands tribute, then sends the Rabshakeh to challenge Jerusalem’s confidence in the LORD and urge its people to surrender; Hezekiah’s officials return with the report.

19.overview: Hezekiah responds to the Assyrian threat by seeking Isaiah’s counsel and spreading Sennacherib’s letter before the LORD in prayer. Isaiah declares the LORD’s judgment against Sennacherib and protection of Jerusalem, and the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp before Sennacherib returns to Nineveh and is killed by his sons.

20.overview: Hezekiah falls gravely ill, prays to the LORD, and receives a promise of healing, fifteen more years of life, and deliverance for Jerusalem, confirmed by the shadow’s return on Ahaz’s stairway. After Hezekiah shows Babylonian envoys his treasures, Isaiah foretells their removal to Babylon and the exile of Hezekiah’s descendants, and Hezekiah dies as Manasseh succeeds him.

sections.heading: The sign of the returning shadow

21.overview: Manasseh reigns in Judah, installs idolatrous worship in Jerusalem and the temple, and leads the people into evil; the LORD announces judgment on Jerusalem through the prophets. After Manasseh dies, Amon succeeds him, continues his idolatry, and is killed by his servants, after which the people make his son Josiah king.

22.overview: Josiah reigns in Jerusalem and orders repairs to the temple, where Hilkiah discovers the Book of the Law and Shaphan reads it to the king. Josiah sends officials to consult Huldah, who announces calamity for Judah but says Josiah will die in peace and not see it.

sections.heading: Temple Repairs and the Book’s Discovery

23.overview: Josiah renews the covenant after the Book of the Covenant is read aloud, removes idolatrous objects and shrines throughout Judah and Samaria, and celebrates a Passover in Jerusalem. Although his reform is praised, the LORD’s judgment against Judah remains; Josiah dies at Megiddo, and Pharaoh Neco deposes Jehoahaz and installs Jehoiakim, whose reign is marked by evil.

24.overview: Nebuchadnezzar subjugates Jehoiakim, and raiders attack Judah as the LORD’s judgment for its sins, including the innocent blood shed under Manasseh. After Jehoiachin’s brief reign, Babylon besieges Jerusalem, takes the king and many inhabitants into exile, removes the temple and palace treasures, and installs Zedekiah, who also rebels against Babylon.

25.overview: Nebuchadnezzar’s army besieges Jerusalem, captures Zedekiah, destroys the city and temple, and takes Judah’s people and officials into exile. Gedaliah governs the remnant until Ishmael kills him and the people flee to Egypt, while Babylon’s king later releases Jehoiachin and grants him a place at the royal table.
